title: Duplicate retry - a double-click and a timeout retry produce exactly one external instruction
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `duplicate-retry` (retry or double-click after submission suppressed by the stable idempotency key; exactly one external instruction exists). Exercises the charter #16 substrate and v3 invariant 20's vocabulary.

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. Draft rules that a suppressed duplicate returns the ORIGINAL handle and status (duplicate_suppressed receipt), and the timeline shows one instruction with the retry annotated - never a second external row. Re-signed 2026-08-21 under the prompt-5 signature sitting (rulings CD-4c, CD-4b); amendment machine-derived from the generation-4 engine's own evaluation and approved by the captain's merge of the amendment PR.

trigger.description: Advisor enters the $75,000 request; after approval the operations user double-clicks Execute, and a network timeout triggers one automatic retry.
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD; execution attempted three times client/transport-side (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Balance 420000 USD; reserve satisfied - this case is about execution integrity, not evaluation.
Six-month reserve (48000 USD) preserved after the movement.

expectedAuthority.note: Standard Firm A dual approval above 25000 USD.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: Approvals recorded; revalidation passes. The idempotency key is derived from the decision, NOT the click, so every duplicate attempt carries the same key.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: A taxable source account was selected; a retirement account is never chosen silently.
After this movement the household still holds its policy-required months of planned withdrawals.
The amount exceeds the firm's dual-approval threshold, so distinct approvers are required before execution.

commentaryNodes.summary: The execution step's idempotency key is a pure function of the approved decision, so a double-click or transport retry cannot mint a new instruction.
The second and third attempts return the original handle with a duplicate_suppressed receipt; the timeline shows ONE external instruction with the retries annotated against it.

commentaryNote: Demoted from the binding explanation set to non-binding commentary by the captain's CD-4b ruling (2026-08-21). Retained as signed intent; describes lifecycle behavior outside the prompt-5 decision engine or comparative context the engine does not emit.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: Evaluation snapshots pinned into the bundle.
Proceed decision with dual-approval authority and an execution plan carrying the stable idempotency key.
Liquidity reservation created before the first attempt.
Second, distinct operations approver approves; quorum satisfied.

Exactly ONE ExecutionStarted is recorded for the step: the duplicate attempts are absorbed by the idempotency key and return duplicate_suppressed receipts referencing the same entry - no second start is ever recorded.
The single external instruction is accepted; the same handle answers all three attempts.
Returned status observed as submitted - once, for the one real instruction.

expectedVerificationState.note: Retries do not create duplicate instructions - provable against the fake adapter now, re-proven against the real sandbox when the trigger fires (demo-contract §8). Execution/status carry fake-adapter-response provenance until then.
